prompt:
You are a senior financial analyst on the Consumer Staples coverage team at a sell-side research firm. The head of research has asked you to prepare a quarterly variance analysis for Procter & Gamble Co (PG) covering the first three quarters of fiscal year 2026. This analysis will feed into the firm's upcoming earnings preview note and will be reviewed by the head of research before publication.

Materials provided:
- Quarterly financial data for Procter & Gamble Co (ticker: PG, CIK: 0000080424) sourced from SEC EDGAR XBRL filings, covering revenues, cost of goods sold, operating income, net income, assets, liabilities, EPS (diluted), R&D expense, and SG&A expense across Q1, Q2, and Q3 of FY2026, with select prior-year comparatives.

Task requirements:
1. Build an Excel workbook with the following tabs:
   - 'Inputs': Raw quarterly data extracted from the source material, organized by line item (Revenue, COGS, Operating Income, Net Income, EPS Diluted, SG&A, R&D, Assets, Liabilities). Include columns for Q1 FY2026, Q2 FY2026, and Q3 FY2026. For Q3, use the three-month period values (the smaller of the two reported figures per quarter).
   - 'Analysis': A variance analysis showing quarter-over-quarter changes (Q2 vs Q1, Q3 vs Q2) for revenue, COGS, operating income, and net income. Calculate both absolute dollar change and percentage change. Include a section computing gross margin, operating margin, and net margin for each quarter.
   - 'Summary': A narrative summary (as merged text cells) that addresses:
     a) The overall revenue trend across Q1-Q3 FY2026.
     b) The largest absolute dollar variance among the four income statement line items between any two consecutive quarters.
     c) Whether operating margins expanded or contracted Q3 vs Q2, and by how many basis points.
     d) The relationship between EPS trends and net income trends.

2. Use three-month period figures for each quarter (i.e., for Q3 FY2026, use the smaller reported values: Revenue = 21,235,000,000, COGS = 10,722,000,000, Operating Income = 4,576,000,000, Net Income = 3,932,000,000, SG&A = 5,936,000,000). For Q2, use Revenue = 22,208,000,000, COGS = 10,834,000,000, Operating Income = 5,366,000,000, Net Income = 4,319,000,000, SG&A = 6,008,000,000. For Q1, use the single reported values.
3. Format all dollar values in billions with two decimal places (e.g., 21.24). Percentage changes should be shown to one decimal place. Margins should be expressed in basis points.
4. All formulas must be live Excel formulas referencing the Inputs sheet. No hard-coded results in the Analysis or Summary sheets.

Deliverable specification:
- Submit a single Excel workbook (.xlsx) with three tabs: Inputs, Analysis, Summary.
- The workbook filename should be 'PG_Q3FY2026_Variance_Analysis.xlsx'.

cells.value: Procter & Gamble Co (PG) - Quarterly Financial Data
Source: SEC EDGAR XBRL | Ticker: PG | CIK: 0000080424
Operating Margin Q3 vs Q2 Change (bps)
Procter & Gamble Co (PG) - Q3 FY2026 Variance Analysis Summary

Revenue declined sequentially across all three quarters: from $22.386B in Q1 to $22.208B in Q2 (a decline of $0.178B or -0.8%) and further to $21.235B in Q3 (a decline of $0.973B or -4.4%). The Q3 decline was materially larger than Q2, representing the most significant sequential revenue contraction in the period. Total revenue for the first three quarters was $65.829B.

The largest absolute dollar variance between consecutive quarters was in Revenue: Q3 vs Q2 showed a decline of $0.973B (from $22.208B to $21.235B). This exceeded all other line-item variances including the Q3 vs Q2 operating income decline of $0.790B (from $5.366B to $4.576B).
Operating Margin Change Q3 vs Q2

Operating margins contracted Q3 vs Q2. Q2 operating margin was 24.16% (Operating Income of $5.366B on Revenue of $22.208B). Q3 operating margin was 21.55% (Operating Income of $4.576B on Revenue of $21.235B). This represents a contraction of approximately 261 basis points. The margin compression was driven by revenue declining faster than operating expenses.

EPS diluted and net income moved in the same direction across all quarters. Net income declined from $4.750B in Q1 to $4.319B in Q2 to $3.932B in Q3. Similarly, EPS diluted declined from $1.95 to $1.78 to $1.63. The percentage declines were roughly parallel: net income fell -9.1% Q2 vs Q1 and -9.0% Q3 vs Q2, while EPS fell -8.7% Q2 vs Q1 and -8.4% Q3 vs Q2, suggesting a relatively stable share count.
